section_suggestions.title: Background
section_suggestions.guidance: General overview of this entity's role and significance in the investigation.

curation.lead:
Essa Abdulfattah Kazim is a senior Emirati financial-markets official who, on 13 February 2026, became Chairman of DP World, the Dubai-government global ports operator, succeeding Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem after bin Sulayem resigned over correspondence disclosed in the U.S. Department of Justice Epstein file release [Finding #11207][DOJ:Epstein-Release-2026-02]. Kazim concurrently holds Governor of the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) since January 2014, Chairman of Borse Dubai, board director of Nasdaq, Inc. (the U.S.-listed exchange operator), board member of Nasdaq Dubai, Vice Chairman of e& (formerly Etisalat Group), board member of Etisalat, and seats on the UAE Free Zones Council, the Securities & Commodities Authority Higher Committee, the Dubai Supreme Fiscal Committee, and the Supreme Legislation Committee (Deputy Chairman) [Finding #11207].

The Nasdaq, Inc. board seat traces to Borse Dubai's 2007 acquisition of a minority stake in the U.S. exchange operator as part of the cross-shareholding settlement of the Borse Dubai/Nasdaq/OMX three-way transaction, which gave the Dubai government persistent representation on the Nasdaq board through whoever chairs Borse Dubai [Finding #11207]. Kazim previously served as Director-General of the Dubai Financial Market from 1999 to 2006 and Chairman of DFM from 2007 to 2021 [Finding #11207]. The combination places a single individual atop Dubai's exchange operator, its principal financial free-zone regulator, the federal capital-markets supervisor, and a U.S.-listed stock-exchange company simultaneously [Finding #11207].

One reading of the succession is that the bin Sulayem-to-Kazim handover at DP World separates an Epstein-correspondent executive from the company while leaving the structural reach of the Tahnoon-aligned Abu Dhabi and Dubai network intact — including U.S.-market access through the Nasdaq board seat, which the successor carries by virtue of the Borse Dubai chairmanship [Finding #11207]. That reading is an analytic inference; Kazim himself is not named in the released DOJ Epstein correspondence [DOJ:Epstein-Release-2026-02].
curation.system_role: Kazim occupies the listing-and-regulatory layer of the Tahnoon-aligned Dubai/Abu Dhabi financial architecture: he simultaneously sits on the Nasdaq, Inc. board (via Borse Dubai's 2007 OMX-Nasdaq cross-holding), governs the DIFC free zone where many Gulf cross-border vehicles incorporate, and chairs Borse Dubai, giving one individual continuous oversight across the U.S. listing venue, the local exchange, and the local regulator.

sections.title: Concurrent Roles
sections.content:
Kazim's 2026 portfolio of positions concentrates exchange-operating, regulatory, free-zone, and telecommunications mandates within a single individual. As of February 2026 he chairs DP World, governs the Dubai International Financial Centre, chairs Borse Dubai (the holding company for the Dubai Financial Market and Nasdaq Dubai), sits on the board of Nasdaq, Inc., serves as Vice Chairman of e& (the UAE federal-controlled telecoms operator formerly known as Etisalat Group) and on the board of Etisalat, holds membership on the UAE Free Zones Council and the Securities & Commodities Authority Higher Committee, and serves on the Dubai Supreme Fiscal Committee and as Deputy Chairman of the Supreme Legislation Committee [Finding #11207].

His prior career was concentrated in Dubai exchange administration: Director-General of the Dubai Financial Market from 1999 to 2006, then Chairman of DFM from 2007 to 2021, before his appointments to DIFC Governor (January 2014, retained alongside DFM chairmanship until 2021) and Borse Dubai Chairman [Finding #11207]. The DP World chairmanship in February 2026 is the first operating-company executive role outside the financial-markets and free-zone perimeter [Finding #11207].

sections.title: Succession at DP World, February 2026
sections.content:
On 13 February 2026 Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem resigned as DP World Group Chairman and Group CEO; Kazim was named Chairman and Yuvraj Narayan, the company's former Chief Financial Officer, was named Group CEO [Finding #11207]. According to contemporaneous reporting cited in the linked Sultan bin Sulayem dossier, the resignation followed the U.S. Department of Justice Epstein file release of February 2026, in which Representative Thomas Massie identified bin Sulayem on 9 February 2026 as a recipient of Jeffrey Epstein's 24 April 2009 email referencing a "torture video" [DOJ:Epstein-Release-2026-02][DOJ:Massie-Disclosure-2026-02-09]. Records in the release additionally indicate that Epstein acted as an intermediary in 2009 to help bin Sulayem lobby the U.K. government via Peter Mandelson regarding the GBP 1.8 billion London Gateway port project [DOJ:Epstein-Release-2026-02]. Canadian pension manager La Caisse paused a stated five-billion-plus deployment alongside DP World contemporaneously with the resignation [DOJ:Epstein-Release-2026-02].

The succession reads as the first visible setback for the Sheikh Tahnoon-aligned UAE corporate cluster arising from Epstein-related exposure, an assessment that places it alongside the November 2025 OpenAI board resignation of Lawrence Summers, according to cross-referenced analysis of the broader case [Finding #11236]. Kazim is not named in the released DOJ Epstein correspondence [DOJ:Epstein-Release-2026-02][Finding #11183].

sections.title: Borse Dubai and the Nasdaq, Inc. Board Seat
sections.content:
Kazim's directorship on the board of Nasdaq, Inc. — the U.S.-listed parent company of the Nasdaq Stock Market — derives from the 2007 three-way cross-holding transaction in which Borse Dubai acquired a minority equity interest in Nasdaq as part of the contested takeover of OMX, the Nordic exchange operator [Finding #11207]. Borse Dubai's chairmanship has carried board representation at Nasdaq, Inc. since the close of that transaction, giving the Dubai government continuous director-level presence at a U.S. self-regulatory-organization parent regardless of changes in the underlying shareholding [Finding #11207].

This arrangement supports an interpretation in which the substitution at DP World is accepted while structural U.S.-market access through the Nasdaq board seat is preserved or extended in the person of Kazim, who carries the seat by virtue of his Borse Dubai chairmanship [Finding #11207]. That interpretation is an inference rather than a documented intent. Independent verification of the current size and form of the Borse Dubai shareholding in Nasdaq, Inc. should be undertaken against Nasdaq's most recent definitive proxy statement (DEF 14A) and Schedule 13G filings on EDGAR [EDGAR:NDAQ-DEF14A].

sections.title: Multi-Layer Regulatory Position
sections.content:
The combination of DIFC Governor, Borse Dubai Chairman, Securities & Commodities Authority Higher Committee member, Free Zones Council member, and now DP World Chairman places Kazim in a position where the same individual oversees the Dubai financial free zone in which many of DP World's holding subsidiaries are domiciled and the exchange holding company on which DP World's Nasdaq Dubai-listed sukuk historically traded [Finding #11207]. The DP World Chairman role thereby overlaps with DIFC governance of DP World's DIFC-registered subsidiaries [Finding #11207].

Kazim's e& Vice Chairmanship and Etisalat board membership extend the perimeter to UAE federal telecommunications, where e& (formerly Etisalat Group) holds significant cross-border digital infrastructure positions [Finding #11207]. The aggregation across exchange, free zone, federal regulator, telecommunications carrier, and ports operator within one individual is, the analysis suggests, a structural feature of a broader Abu Dhabi-Dubai consolidation of sovereign, commercial, and regulatory functions [Finding #11236].

sections.title: Position in the Tahnoon-Aligned Cluster
sections.content:
Analysis of the post-Epstein UAE re-platforming destination describes it as a network of vehicles aligned with Sheikh Tahnoon's commercial portfolio, including MGX, Aryam Investment 1, World Liberty Financial, and the recently OCC-approved Erebor Bank [Finding #11236]. On that account, the cluster's identifying feature is the recombination of exposed entities into a system governed by lighter-disclosure regimes (ADGM, DIFC, FSRA) rather than a wind-down, according to that assessment [Finding #11236].

Kazim's structural position differs from the operating-company executives of that cluster in that he sits in the regulatory and listing layer rather than acting as a deal-flow principal [Finding #11207]. The same analysis suggests that the bin Sulayem departure paired with the Kazim appointment preserves the Nasdaq board seat — and therefore U.S.-market access — while removing the Epstein-correspondent executive [Finding #11236]. A review of the records indicates that this reading is consistent with the documented role inventory but is not itself established in primary corporate filings to date [Finding #11236].

open_questions: What is the current size and class of Borse Dubai's equity stake in Nasdaq, Inc., and is it disclosed in Nasdaq's most recent definitive proxy (DEF 14A) or any Schedule 13D/13G on EDGAR?

Are any DP World subsidiaries DIFC-registered such that DP World Chairman and DIFC Governor functions covering the same legal entity create a documented conflict of interest under DIFC governance rules?
Does Kazim's Securities & Commodities Authority Higher Committee role include any recusal obligations covering DP World, e&, or Borse Dubai matters, and have any been recorded?
What e& (Etisalat Group) U.S.-touching transactions, FCC filings, or CFIUS reviews has Kazim's Vice Chairmanship overlapped, given e&'s cross-border telecoms positions?

Is there any documentary record (DOJ Epstein release, congressional disclosures, or third-party correspondence) connecting Kazim — as distinct from bin Sulayem — to Jeffrey Epstein or Epstein-network principals?
